tasks.short: Check, resolve and file personnel documents across employment, recruitment, training, performance and leave cases.

steps.what: Inspect personnel documents and identify the case type.

loop.input: Personnel document and allowed case types.
loop.output: Proposed case type, required fields and source passages.
loop.check: Validate field formats, employee identifier and source passages; flag missing or conflicting information.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; unresolved fields go to the HR assistant.
loop.why_not_simpler: Externally supplied documents vary in layout and wording. Structured submissions bypass the loop.

steps.what: Compare case details with the employee record and required evidence.
Request missing documents or corrections from the employee or manager.
Resolve disputed classifications, leave evidence or sensitive case interpretations.
Register the approved case outcome in the personnel record.
File supporting documents with access restrictions and retention labels.
Update the separate personnel case tracker.

tasks.design: Configure case forms, checklists, reminders and approved outcome recording in the {HCM}, with restricted filing in the {DOCS}. A bounded extraction loop proposes fields from variable documents; deterministic checks and an exception queue support review before use. Case status comes from the {HCM}, replacing the separate {SPREADSHEET} tracker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Document variation, inconsistent identifiers and unclear approval routes made reliable filing expensive. Existing configuration often covered only part of the process.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms and permissions handle routine cases. AI-assisted coding can reduce adapter development effort, while bounded extraction handles variable documents without deciding employment outcomes.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed facts, access to grievance records, conflicting policies and effective dates still need careful handling. Extracting a statement does not establish its truth.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when apparently complete paperwork conceals a dispute, coercion or an unresolved employment question.

ambition.what: A personnel case readiness check before a manager submits a change.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from filing and chasing to resolving incomplete cases and helping managers prepare sound submissions. The assistant can return incomplete packets under agreed criteria; employment decisions remain with authorised roles.

reach.task: Prepare a case chronology for a disputed leave or classification request.
reach.learn: Evidence provenance, policy interpretation and escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: Employee self-service and configured HR change workflows are available today.
Bounded document extraction, validation and exception routing are established patterns; HR-specific accuracy needs testing.
GDPR Article 22 requires assessment when automation makes decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured HR case results.

assumptions: Routine cases skip the exception decision; shares represent a blended workload.
Personnel case processing and employee field updates share intake components; savings must not be added twice.
Access restrictions, data minimisation and retention rules apply under GDPR.
Build ranges cover one initial deployment using reusable case templates and customer-specific configuration.
Consent and access estimates include national consultation requirements where applicable; elapsed time may be longer.
unknowns: Which document types dominate the workload?
Which case approvals and retention schedules are already configured?
Can the existing systems enforce separate access for grievances and health-related records?
How much work is duplicated in a separate case tracker?
research_questions: Which retention and employee consultation requirements apply under relevant national rules?
What extraction error rate is acceptable for each document class?
new_work: Review extracted fields and ambiguous employee matches.
Maintain case checklists, access groups and retention labels.
Resolve failed filing operations and monitor overdue exceptions.

tasks.short: Update employee data from approved changes, payroll outputs, operational records and supervisory reports.

steps.what: Read employee and manager requests for personnel data changes.
Retrieve approved earnings data for personnel record updates.
Retrieve attributable production or sales totals where personnel records require them.
Match employee identifiers, reporting periods and effective dates in the update workbook.
Enter approved address, absence and other routine employee field changes.
Attach the approved supervisory report to the employee performance record.
Record the authorised termination date and reason.
Check saved fields against the approved change set.
Confirm completion to the authorised requester.

tasks.design: Configure authenticated change forms and field ownership in the {HCM}; use deterministic adapters for required data from the {PAYROLL} and {OPS_SYSTEM}. Match identifiers and effective dates before writing, preserve source references, and link approved reports in the {TALENT}. Reconcile writes automatically and gate termination activation with the HR specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate identifiers, effective dates and batch exports made copying easier than maintaining reliable interfaces. Unclear field ownership encouraged duplicate records.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured self-service handles routine changes, and reusable adapters can enforce matching, validation and replay protection. AI-assisted coding can shorten implementation without introducing a model into record updates.
tasks.still_hard: Retroactive corrections, rehires, multiple contracts and termination reversals complicate effective dating. Some earnings and production fields may have no valid reason to be duplicated.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve conflicting authoritative sources and recognise when a routine-looking update could wrongly affect employment or pay.

ambition.what: A daily correction queue for conflicting employee effective dates.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends more time resolving source conflicts and less time copying values. They can request corrections from source owners under agreed rules; they gain no authority to change pay or decide termination.

reach.task: Investigate employee master-data differences before a pay run.
reach.learn: Effective dating, payroll cutoffs and correction versus reversal.

evidence.claim: Configured HR self-service changes can flow into payroll.
Identifier matching, effective-date checks and write reconciliation can use deterministic code.
The proposed workflow records authorised outcomes rather than making termination or performance decisions.
Time shares, remaining effort and delivery ranges are estimates requiring local validation.

assumptions: Source retrieval steps apply only to employee groups needing those fields.
Earnings are copied from approved results; the assistant does not calculate payroll.
The example company uses the {OPS_SYSTEM} for attributable output; other companies may use the {CRM}.
The structured-data prior supports deterministic updates; system screens receive more weight than the supplied document-time prior.
Routine changes use authenticated requests and existing approvals where required.
Unnecessary duplicate fields should be removed after confirming recordkeeping needs.
National consultation requirements and access provisioning are included where applicable.
unknowns: Which employee fields must legally and operationally be retained?
Which system is authoritative for each field?
Are reliable employee identifiers and effective-dated interfaces available?
Do termination updates trigger account removal or other downstream actions?
How often do retroactive corrections and rehires occur?
research_questions: Which national recordkeeping duties require earnings or production data in personnel records?
Which adapter patterns safely handle multiple concurrent employment contracts?
new_work: Resolve identifier, period and effective-date exceptions.
Maintain source ownership and field mappings.
Check interface failures, duplicate events and unauthorised field changes.
Review termination activation and downstream reconciliation.

tasks.short: Explain personnel policies, benefits and procedures to employees and applicants.

steps.what: Read the question and establish its topic and audience.
Find the current policy, benefit terms and applicable procedure.
Check relevant employment facts for an authenticated employee.
Write and send a routine policy explanation.

loop.input: Question, current approved sources and minimum permitted employment context.
loop.output: Plain-language explanation with source references and unresolved points.
loop.check: Require valid source references, matching policy dates and audience permissions; the HR assistant checks meaning before sending.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing or conflicting sources produce a referral rather than an answer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover common questions, but varied questions need a short explanation combining several policy passages.

steps.what: Discuss sensitive circumstances and check that the person understands their options.
Refer unresolved interpretations or exception requests to the HR specialist.
Record the answer, referral and follow-up status.

tasks.design: Use a topic form in the {HELPDESK}, a versioned policy index in the {DOCS} and permission-limited context from the {HCM}. Approved templates handle standard questions; a bounded loop drafts explanations for review before sending through the {EMAIL}. Sensitive conversations remain human, while referrals and case records follow configured workflows.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policies were scattered, versions were unclear and answers depended on individual knowledge. Searching faster alone did not ensure the correct policy applied.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned retrieval, reusable answer templates and bounded drafting can prepare an explanation with traceable sources. Existing request workflows handle routing and follow-up.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting agreements, unusual personal circumstances and exceptions require interpretation. A technically correct answer can still be poorly understood or distressing.
tasks.human_edge: Notice hesitation, explain practical consequences and help someone ask the question they were reluctant to raise.

ambition.what: An asynchronous policy question service for employees working outside office hours.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time searching and more time explaining choices and resolving unclear cases. They can publish reviewed routine explanations within their remit; they cannot grant policy exceptions.

reach.task: Turn recurring policy questions into clearer employee guidance.
reach.learn: Policy interpretation, accessible writing and distinguishing explanation from individual advice.

evidence.claim: HR policy answering from collective agreement material is offered today.
Knowledge-based answering with a prefilled request when no answer is available is offered today.
Direct AI interaction requires the applicable transparency disclosure.
The proposed time savings and service design are estimates; support-centre case results do not establish HR outcomes.

assumptions: Shares blend routine written answers, conversations and referrals; each question need not follow every branch.
A topic form replaces routine intake sorting; unclassified questions enter the human queue.
Applicants receive public policy information without access to employee records.
The first deployment reviews generated explanations before sending.
GDPR access and minimisation requirements apply; national employment rules affect interpretation.
A direct employee-facing AI interface would disclose that it uses AI.
unknowns: Who approves policy versions and resolves conflicting guidance?
Which agreements and employee groups require different answers?
How many questions need personal context or a conversation?
Can employees outside office hours access an authenticated request channel?
research_questions: How should answer evaluation measure omission of exceptions and misleading simplification?
Which national rules constrain individual benefit or employment advice?
new_work: Review generated explanations and maintain approved answer templates.
Inspect unanswered questions and referral delays.
Test permissions and source references after policy changes.

tasks.short: Support benefit enrolments and occupational injury claims through checks, submissions, reconciliation and employee assistance.

steps.what: Inspect benefit elections or administrative occupational injury claim forms.
Check employment facts, submission deadlines and required administrative evidence.
Resolve discretionary enrolments, disputed coverage or ambiguous claim requirements.
Prepare the provider submission using approved administrative information.
Submit the enrolment or administrative claim to the provider.
Record approved contribution changes for payroll processing.
Reconcile pending requests, provider acknowledgements and contribution instructions.
Discuss missing acknowledgements or disputed administrative details with the provider.
Send the employee a factual status update and next steps.

tasks.design: Configure structured requests in the {HCM} and deadline checks in the {WORKFLOW}; generate provider forms from approved fields in the {DOCS}. A deterministic adapter submits through the {PARTNER_PORTAL} after approval and sends authorised contribution instructions to the {PAYROLL}. Reconciliation and factual status notices replace the separate {SPREADSHEET} tracker, while coverage disputes remain with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Provider-specific forms, submission routes and payroll cutoffs fragmented administration. Claim status often depended on manual follow-up.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured capture, template generation and reusable adapters cover much of the work without a model. AI-assisted coding can reduce the cost of provider-specific mappings and reconciliation.
tasks.still_hard: Providers may lack supported interfaces. Coverage disputes, retroactive elections and occupational injury procedures depend on scheme terms and national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Help an injured or worried employee navigate the process without presenting an administrative check as a coverage decision.

ambition.what: A deadline rescue service for incomplete benefit enrolments.

tasks.altitude: The assistant follows up on cases at risk of missing deadlines and supports employees through exceptions. They can prioritise administrative rescue work; they gain no authority to adjudicate claims or change coverage.

reach.role: Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialist
reach.task: Investigate a contribution or enrolment mismatch between employer and provider records.
reach.learn: Scheme eligibility, contribution effective dates and provider escalation routes.

evidence.claim: HR self-service changes flowing to payroll demonstrate part of the proposed administrative pattern.
The digest does not establish end-to-end benefit or occupational injury claim automation.
Structured forms, deterministic validation and template generation can prepare administrative submissions without adjudicating claims.
GDPR requires appropriate grounds and safeguards for processing health-related information.
Build ranges and remaining effort are estimates conditional on provider access.

assumptions: Occupational injury administration follows the relevant national scheme; a US workers' compensation process is not assumed.
Shares blend benefit enrolments and administrative injury claims; not every case needs every branch.
Medical evidence goes directly to the authorised provider or designated restricted service where appropriate.
Generic HR case records contain only necessary administrative information.
A supported provider interface or accepted structured submission route exists for the estimated integration.
The contribution instruction enters existing payroll controls and does not execute a pay run.
Access and consultation estimates include national requirements where applicable.
unknowns: Which benefit schemes, providers and national injury processes apply?
Which provider interfaces or batch submissions are available?
Who may approve submissions and discretionary enrolments?
Where is medical evidence currently stored and who may access it?
Which payroll cutoffs and provider acknowledgement delays cause failures?
research_questions: Which national occupational injury reporting deadlines and consultation duties apply?
Which lawful grounds and safeguards cover each health-related data flow?
Which provider submission methods support reliable acknowledgement and duplicate prevention?
new_work: Maintain scheme rules, templates, deadlines and contribution mappings.
Investigate missing acknowledgements and contribution mismatches.
Review restricted access and remove unnecessary sensitive information.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward resolving record conflicts, preparing sound cases and explaining procedures. Administrative correction rights can expand within agreed limits; employment, benefit and claim decisions stay with authorised decision-makers.
reach: Human Resources Specialists: prepare evidence-based case chronologies and clearer policy guidance.
Payroll and Timekeeping Clerks: investigate effective-date and employee master-data mismatches.
Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialists: reconcile provider enrolments and contribution instructions.
skills_to_grow: Effective dating, source ownership and record reconciliation.
Privacy-aware document handling and permission design.
Reviewing extracted fields and source-backed explanations.
Policy interpretation, employee communication and escalation.
Maintaining workflow rules and investigating integration failures.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a personnel administration readiness service that catches incomplete cases, conflicting dates and approaching benefit deadlines before they harm employees. Reusable templates provide a head start across employers, with local policies, access and national rules configured for each deployment.

job.title: Human Resources Assistants, Except Payroll and Timekeeping
